Empty when none was deposited, which is not evidence that the researcher had no role in the award. Detail view only. output.funding.contributors description: One deposited contributor, carrying only the fields deposited. output.funding.contributors.name output.funding.contributors.name description: Credit name, as deposited. output.funding.contributors.orcidId output.funding.contributors.orcidId description: The contributor's ORCID iD, when deposited. output.funding.contri orcid_get_profile: description, inputSchema, outputSchema -and -profile. +profile, public email addresses with their verified flags, and countries. +Set include_history for the record's trust signals: when and how it was created, whether the researcher claimed it, and whether it has a verified email, private addresses included. parameters: +input.include_history input.include_history default: false input.include_history description: Also return the record's history. Reads ORCID's full record instead of the person section; for a researcher with many works that upstream response can exceed 10 MB, and the first call for such a record can time out while ORCID builds it, so call again after a timeout. This tool still returns only the profile and its history. Set it only when the trust signals are needed. +output.emails.verified output.emails.verified description: Whether ORCID marks the address verified, exactly as published; absent orcid_get_research_resources: outputSchema parameters: -Note when no research resources are found — this section +Notes on this answer, in order: that the iD could not be checked for a merge into another iD (an empty result -sparsely populated across ORCID profiles — or when +then unconfirmed; call again), that -iD. +iD, and that no research resources were found — this section is sparsely populated across ORCID profiles. orcid_get_work_detail: outputSchema parameters: -Deprecated-iD +Notes on this answer, in order: that the iD could not be checked for a merge into another iD (put-codes that did not resolve are then unconfirmed; call again), the deprecated-iD orcid_resolve_researcher: description, inputSchema, outputSchema -signals: +signals — -query. +query — plus the other names listed on each record. -record. +record; when no name query finds a record with it, each anchor is tried alone and the notice says the candidates were found by the anchor alone. The ranking covers only the candidates returned: when totalFound is larger, the notice gives the rows value that ranks more and the orcid_search_researchers call that lists the rest, without match signals. parameters: -record. +record, matched in any letter case and whether the record holds it bare or as one of those forms. +The ranking covers only these: totalFound counts every record matching queryUsed, and when it is larger the notice says how to reach the rest. +output.candidates.otherNames output.candidates.otherNames description: Other names listed on the ORCID record. output.candidates.otherNames description: Alternative name. -Requested/effective +One string joining, in order: the requested/effective +cap; that the candidates were found by a DOI or PMID anchor alone, no record matching the name with orcid_search_researchers: inputSchema parameters: -record. +record, matched in any letter case and whether the record holds it bare or as one of those forms.

entry.content: tendon_design: description, inputSchema +Creep and shrinkage take the humidity, cement class and drying age from the concrete's time-dependent material, and in mode improve the age at stressing from the construction stages (concreteAge says what was used); forces.prestressFrom civil checks the model's tendons with CIVIL NX's own staged prestress. Span-by-span decks of coupled draped tendons are read as such (no cantilever tendons). parameters: +input.forces.prestressFrom input.forces.prestressFrom default: "plugin" input.forces.prestressFrom description: mode improve on a staged model: the prestress the checks use. civil = the force, P·e and secondary moment from CIVIL NX's construction-stage results (the real erection sequence, couplers, creep), while the tendons stay as the model has them; plugin = the plugin's own losses and secondary moment on the finished continuous girder. Output prestressInChecks says which was used and why. input.forces.prestressFrom enum: ["plugin", "civil"] +input.losses.cementClass input.losses.cementClas

Returns title, repo, url, labels and updated time per bounty, plus the total count. x402-csv-build: description +CSV text from row objects: pass rows as -CSV from data. +JSON array of objects (or a JSON array string); keys of the first row become the header, values are RFC 4180 quoted so commas, quotes and line breaks survive the round trip. An empty list returns an empty string. x402-csv-sort: description -data +rows -specified column. Provide csv text +named column (column= or col=): numeric columns compare numerically, others lexicographically; order=desc reverses it. RFC 4180 quoting is parsed on the way in -column (or col); optional order=desc for descending. +re-quoted on the way out, so the sorted CSV stays valid. x402-csv-stats: description -Compute +Column-by-column -data. +data: every header whose values parse as numbers gets count, min, max, sum, average and median; RFC 4180 quoting is parsed first so a comma inside a quoted cell does not shift the columns being measured. x402-funding-rate: description -Perpetual +Binance USDT-perpetual futures +Pass symbol=BTCUSDT or any Binance perp pair (default BTCUSDT); returns the latest fundingRate, its fundingTime, and the sign convention (positive = longs pay shorts). One 8-hour window per call. x402-mean-of: description -Mean +Arithmetic mean -of. +a list of numbers. Pass values=1,2,3,4 as a comma list or repeated param; returns result with the average (2.5 for that list). x402-sum-of-squares: description +the squares -squares. +a list of numbers. Pass values=1,2,3,4 as a comma list or repeated param; returns result = 1^2+2^2+3^2+4^2 (30 for that list).

entry.content: employer_cost: description, inputSchema, outputSchema +When the user asks for the full cost through an Employer of Record and has been quoted its fees, pass them as the user gives them (eor_fee_monthly, eor_one_time_fees, deposit): the answer keeps the statutory cost, the fees entered by the user and their total apart, and the deposit out of the total. EOR Scope holds no provider fee: without the user's figures, the answer stays statutory, and eor_fee_sources says where each provider publishes its fees. -tax, +tax or -advice, or for the fees of a provider. +advice. parameters: +input.deposit input.deposit description: A deposit the user was quoted: shown apart, never added to the cost input.deposit.amount input.deposit.amount description: Deposit or reserve the user was asked for input.deposit.currency input.deposit.currency default: "USD" input.deposit.currency description: USD, or the local currency of the country input.deposit.currency enum: ["USD", "local"] input.eor_fee_monthly input.eor_fee_monthly description: The Employer of Record fee the user was quoted, per employee per month, in fees_currency. Only a figure the user gives. input.eor_one_time_fees input.e list_countries: description, inputSchema, outputSchema +Also use it when the user asks in which countries hiring costs the employer the least in statutory charges (e.g. "countries where employer charges are smallest for a 60k hire", "pays où les charges patronales sont les plus faibles"): pass salary_usd and sort_by "statutory_employer_charge" to order the countries by statutory employer charge at equal salary, from the smallest. A country whose total is declared "at least" or "at most" at that salary is listed apart, never ordered among totals. The order covers statutory charges only, before any Employer of Record fee. parameters: +input.salary_usd input.salary_usd description: Gross annual salary in USD, the same in every country: each country then gets its statutory employer charge at that salary input.sort_by input.sort_by default: "name" input.sort_by description: "name" (alphabetical, default) or "statutory_employer_charge": statutory employer charge at equal salary, from the smallest; needs salary_usd input.sort_by enum: ["name", "statutory_employer_charge"] output.bounded_not_ordered +output.countries.statutory_employer_charge_at_salary output.countries.statutory_employer_charge_at_salary.annual output.countries. added eor_fee_sources

entry.content: offers_stock: description, inputSchema +The whole offer list comes by default; `page` returns it ten offers at a time. -Billed +On an account, a call is billed -lookup, which is +page of the offer list it delivers, plus the cart checks of check_inventory. Amazon lists ten offers a page, so an ASIN with up to ten offers is one request and each further page of its list is one -than +(a listing with 35 offers: 4). `page` (1, 2, ...) returns that page alone for +request +-- page 1 is the buy-box offer and the first ten of the list -- and each row then carries `page` and `total_pages`. A page past the end is answered like a not-found it parameters: +The filter covers the buy-box offer too: it is in the answer only when its own condition is among those asked for. +input.page input.page default: null input.page description: One page of each ASIN's offer list instead of the whole list. Amazon lists ten offers a page, in its own order (it starts from the lowest price with delivery); page 1 also carries the buy-box offer. One request per ASIN whatever the listing's size, and each row then says `page` and `total_pages`. Omit for the whole list, which is one request per page of ten. input.page title: Page search: description, inputSchema -1); +1; "21+ used & new offers" reads 21); `product_minimum_offer_price` is the price on the card's "More Buying Choices" line -- the lowest among the listing's other offers, new or used -- a decimal string, null when the card shows no such line; under product_condition=USED the answer carries `price_note`, which says which price is which, and offers_stock with the USED_* conditions returns the used offers themselves; parameters: +USED lists products that have a used offer: `product_price` stays the featured offer's price (usually a new item's) and `product_minimum_offer_price` is the lowest price among the listing's other offers.
